title: 38% Discount With a Missing Strategic Flag and a Superseded Tier Table
scenario_text:
You are on Deal Desk at Freya Systems, a B2B analytics SaaS vendor. AE Roman Dietz is closing an expansion with Gjallarhorn Media at a 38% list discount and wants the approval path locked before quarter-end.

Active policy: Discount Policy DPG v7, effective 2025-06-01. Discount tiers by depth: 0-20% Sales Director; 21-35% VP Sales; 36-50% CRO plus a written margin memo. Exception: a current strategic-account designation lets VP Sales approve up to 50% without CRO involvement. DPG v7 restructured the tiers from DPG v6 (0-25% Director; 26-40% VP Sales; above 40% CRO), under which there was no strategic-account provision at all.

Roman forwards two precedents. First, the one he leans on: 2025-03-14, Skirnir Corp, a 38% discount approved directly by VP Sales Lena Pike. Deal-desk log: policy version at decision DPG v6, note 'within VP band (26-40%).' Second: 2025-07-02, Bilskirnir Inc, a 40% discount approved by VP Sales under the DPG v7 strategic-account exception; log note 'strategic-account designated, VP authority to 50%.'

Current Gjallarhorn facts: no strategic-account designation exists on the account, the product configuration is standard, and there are no other atypical terms. Finance confirms nothing else is unusual, that no CRO pre-authorization exists, and that the deal's blended margin sits within the normal range for the product line. The account has been a customer for two years, is not flagged as a named strategic account in the CRM, and carries no executive-sponsor relationship that would support a designation. Roman writes: 'Lena signed 38% for Skirnir herself in March, and she signed 40% for Bilskirnir in July. Either way this sits with the VP - please just route it to Lena so we can paper it before the quarter closes.' The quarter closes in four days and Roman has flagged the deal as commit.
question: What approval is required for Gjallarhorn Media's 38% discount?
choices: VP Sales approval alone, mirroring the Skirnir Corp precedent where the same VP approved an identical 38% discount.
VP Sales approval under the strategic-account exception, since 38% is comfortably within the 50% strategic ceiling that the Bilskirnir deal used.

CRO approval plus a written margin memo, because DPG v7 places 38% in the 36-50% CRO band and Gjallarhorn carries no strategic-account designation; the Skirnir precedent was decided under the superseded DPG v6.
Sales Director approval, since a 38% discount is a routine competitive concession that does not affect contract structure.
No incremental approval, because the AE may match a previously approved discount depth for a comparable account.
